overhead:
## Conductor Name 
The name of the conductor that is currently selected from the list at left. 

## LightTable Device Conductor Size 
The size of the overhead conductor used for coordination in LightTable. Use this field to associate a WindMil overhead conductor to a LightTable overhead conductor. 

## LightTable Device Conductor Type 
The type of the overhead conductor used for coordination in LightTable. Use this field to associate a WindMil overhead conductor to a LightTable overhead conductor. 

## LightTable Button 
Opens LightTable and adds the specified conductor curve to a new LTF file. Note: This button is disabled in WindMilMap.

## Current Carrying Capacity 
The manufacturer's recommended maximum current carrying capacity. 

## Resistance (Ohms/mile) 
Allows you to specify the resistive value to be used in the calculation of the overhead impedance matrices. 

The temperature that WindMil analysis uses can be set in System Preferences. 

## Geometric Mean Radius 
Defines the geometric mean radius of the conductor. 

## Conductor Diameter 
Defines the conductor diameter. This field is required if charging on overhead line is to be calculated. 

## Preferred Neutral 
Specifies the conductor in the EQDB that is to be used as the default neutral conductor for this conductor. This information is used when you have defined a circuit element's phase conductors, but no neutral conductor.
underground:
## Conductor Name 
Lists the name of the conductor currently being edited. 

## LightTable Device Conductor Size 
The size of the corresponding underground conductor used for coordination in LightTable. Use this field to associate a WindMil underground conductor to a LightTable underground conductor. 

## LightTable Device Conductor Type 
The type of the corresponding underground conductor used for coordination in LightTable. Use this field to associate a WindMil underground conductor to a LightTable underground conductor. 

## LightTable Button 
Opens LightTable and adds the specified conductor curve to a new LTF file. Note: This button is disabled in WindMilMap.

## Current Carrying Capacity of Conductor 
The current carrying capacity of the selected conductor. 

## Phase Conductor Resistance 
The phase conductor resistance of the conductor. 

## GMR of Phase Conductor 
The geometric mean radius of the phase conductor. If the geometric mean radius of the phase conductor is not available with the electrical characteristics of the underground cable, use the geometric mean radius from the tables for the appropriate bare conductor. 

## Type Neutral 
Can be either “Concentric”, “Tape Shield”, or “No Concentric”. Concentric should be used for all concentric strand neutrals. 

## Equivalent Neutral Resistance 
The concentric neutral resistance. This value is used only if Concentric is selected for Type Neutral. This is because the resistance of tape shield neutrals is calculated using the thickness of the shield and the basic resistivity of copper. 
## Number of Neutral Strands 

The number of strands in the concentric neutral. This value isused only if Concentric is selected for Type Neutral. 

## OD of Cable Including Neutral 
The outside diameter of the cable, including the concentric neutral or tape shield, but not any jacket external to the concentric neutral or tape shield. 

## Diameter Under Neutral (over screen) 
The diameter of the circle, just under the concentric neutral or tape shield. This diameter will include any semi-conductive jacket or screen over the insulation. The difference between OD of Cable Including Neutral Conductor and Diameter Under Neutral, divided by two, should be the diameter of a concentric neutral strand or the thickness of the tape shield. Analysis warnings and errors may occur if Diameter Under Neutral is equal to or greater than the outside diameter of the cable (including neutral). 

## OD of Cable Insulation (under screen) 
The outside diameter of the cable insulation, not including any semi-conductive jacket or screen. This value should be less than or equal to Diameter Under Neutral. 

## Diameter of Conductor 
Calculates charging on underground line, when the capacitive charging current factor is zero. If used, this value should be less than OD Of Cable Insulation. 

## Dielectric Constant of Insulation 
Calculates charging and is required only if the capacitive charging current factor is zero.
zsm:
## Impedance     
Provides the name of the Zsm impedance definition currently being edited. 

## Current Capacity (Amps) 
Specifies the current-carrying capacity of the Zsm element being defined. This value will be used to define current overload on all circuit elements for which this Zsm impedance definition is selected. 

## Values In 
Determines how the rest of the values are entered based on your choice. The three options are % (in percent), PU (per unit values,) or Ohms (in ohms). 

Changing from one selection to another will result in the recalculation and redisplay of impedance values. For example, if values are in Ohms and Value In is changed to PU, all impedance values will be converted to PU in the specified Base kVA and Base kV. 

## Base kVA 
Specifies the base kVA for the impedance values, which are in % or PU. 

## Base kV 
Specifies the base kV for the impedance values, which are in % or PU. 

*Tip: Changing the Base kVA or Base kV while in % or PU will cause the value in ohms to change.* 

## Units 
Displays and allows selection of the per unit distance. Options are “Total”, “Mile”, “Kilometer”, “1000 ft”, “Feet”, and “Meters”. If “Mile” is selected, the entered impedance values are assumed to be per mile. Thus, the total impedance of an overhead or underground circuit element would be the entered values times the length of the element in miles. When Total is selected, the entered values are assumed to be total for the circuit element. Total can be used for any type of circuit element, but should always be used for the non-length type circuit elements, such as a source. 

## Self 
Displays or enters the self impedance of the conductor in the R and +jX fields. The self admittance for the calculation of charging is entered in the +jB field. 

Entry of sequence values will result in recalculation of the self and mutual values. Entry of the self and mutual values will result in the recalculation of the sequence values. 

## Calculator... 
Defines sequence impedances based on fault duties. This can be useful if you have fault information at a substation, but don't have positive or zero sequence values. Fault current reactance can be entered as either a phase angle in degrees or as an X/R ratio. 

The calculator can also be used to include the impedance of a substation-level transformer in the source definition itself. This is useful if you want to model everything inside the fence as part of the source element.

## Impedance 
Displays the name of the Zabc impedance definition currently being edited. 

## Current Capacity (Amps) 
Defines the amperage rating of this impedance definition. 

## Values In 
Determines how the rest of the values on this page are entered. The three options are % (in percent), PU (per unit values), or Ohms. 

Changing from one selection to another will result in the recalculation and redisplay of impedance values. For example, if values are in Ohms and Values In is changed to PU; all impedance values will be converted to PU in the specified Base kVA and Base kV. 

## Base kVA 
Specifies the base kVA for the impedance values, which are in % or PU. 

## Base kV 
Specifies the base kV for the impedance values, which are in % or PU. 

Changing the Base kVA or Base kV while in % or PU will cause the value in ohms to change. 

## Units 
Displays the per unit distance. Options are “Total”, “Mile”, “Kilometer”, “1000 ft”, and “Feet and Meters”. If “Mile” is selected, the entered impedance values are assumed to be per mile. Thus, the total impedance of an overhead or underground circuit element would be the entered values times the length of the element in miles. When “Total” is selected, the entered values are assumed to be total for the circuit element. Total may be used for any type of circuit element but should always be used for the non-length type circuit elements such as a source. 

## Zabc 
R and +jX fields should be filled with the appropriate self and mutual impedance values.
construction:
## General Notes
GMDP gives the geometric mean distance between phases. The 2-phase GMDP is defined as the distance between the 2-phase conductors. The 3-phase GMDP is defined as the cubed root of the product of the distances A to B, B to C, and C to A. 

GMDPN gives the geometric mean distance between phases and the neutral. The 2-phase GMDPN is defined as the square root of the product of each phase to neutral. The 3-phase GMDPN is defined as the cubed root of the product of the distance A to Neutral, B to Neutral, and C to Neutral. 

For a single-phase line, GMDP and GMDPN are the distance between the phase and the neutral. For an underground line, GMDP gives the geometric mean distance between phase cables. 

# OH Geometry

## Distance from X-Axis to Ground 
The average distance between the ground and the horizontal reference. Units can be selected from the drop-down list. 

## Assume Full Transposition 
If we assume full transposition, lines that use this construction will assume full transposition in impedance calculations. Full transposition will result in all mutual (off diagonal) impedances being equal. 

## Units 
The units that you will use to specify distances. 

## Position 1,2,3 and Neutral 1 and 2 
The distance between a line and the vertical or horizontal references. Distances are assumed to be in the units selected. 

## Position of Conductor(s) If Single Phase 
The position in the drawing that WindMil should assume corresponds to the position of a single-phase wye-connected line element. 

## Position of Conductor(s) If Two Phase 
The position in the drawing that should be assumed if this single-phase delta-connected line element. 

## Parallel Conductor Spacing 
The length of the gap between any two adjacent conductors for a single phase. 

## Parallel Neutral Spacing 
The length of the gap between any two adjacent neutral conductors. 

# Random UG Geometry

## Distance from Surface 
The distance from the ground level to bottom of the trench. Units are as selected from the drop-down list to the right. 

## Average Separation 
The average distance between cable concentric neutrals in units, as selected from the drop-down list to the right. The cable diameter (to concentric neutrals) will be added to this entry to define the Geometric Mean Distance between Phases or GMDP. 

## Parallel Conductor Spacing 
The length of the gap between any two adjacent conductors for a single phase. 

## Parallel Neutral Spacing 
The length of the gap between any two adjacent neutral conductors. 

# Specified UG Geometry

## Assume Full Transposition 
Forces elements using this construction to assume full transposition in impedance calculations. Full transposition will result in all mutual (off diagonal) impedances being equal. 

## Phase A, B, C, and Neutral 
The distance between a line and the vertical or horizontal references. Distances are assumed to be in the units selected. 

## Parallel Conductor Spacing 
The length of the gap between any two adjacent conductors for a single phase. 

## Parallel Neutral Spacing 
The length of the gap between any two adjacent neutral conductors.
overcurrent_device:
## Overcurrent Device 
The name of this device equipment.

## LightTable Control 

The name of the LightTable device object associated with the selected equipment.

## LightTable Operating Device 

The name of an optional secondary device, which is a cutout for Fuses, a recloser for Electronic Reclosers, and a relay for Circuit Breakers. See the LightTable Coordination—Assigning Devices section for more information.

## LightTable Buttons 

These will open LightTable and display the corresponding Control or Operating Device from the device database below. Note: These buttons are disabled in WindMilMap.

## Group 

Defines both the type of device and the coordination method to use. The different specifications are: 

### None, Source, Bay 

Each of these types are ignored by coordination and serve as placeholder devices. 

### OCR 

Defines the device to be a recloser. The type (hydraulic or electronic) is defined by the Device Type drop-down. 

If the upline device is a recloser (OCR or Recloser), then the cycle separation test is used. If the minimum and maximum faults are less than the first (usually the smallest) coordination point, then the devices coordinate. If the faults are between the two points, the devices yield a warning. If the faults are greater than the second (usually the largest) coordination point, then the coordination fails. 

If the upline device is a fuse, then the devices coordinate if the maximum fault is less than the first coordination point. 

If the upline device is a sectionalizer, then the upline device is skipped and the next device upline is considered. 

Any other device is ignored. 

### Recloser 

Defines the device to be a recloser. 

If the upline device is a recloser (OCR or Recloser), then the minimum pickups of the two devices are compared. If the upline device’s pickup is greater than this device, there is good coordination. 

If the upline device is a fuse, then the devices coordinate if the maximum fault is less than the first coordination point. 

If the upline device is a sectionalizer, then the upline device is skipped and the next device upline is considered. 

Any other device is ignored. 

### Fuse 

Defines the device to be a fuse. 

If the upline device is a recloser (OCR or Recloser), then if the minimum fault is greater than the first coordination point and the maximum fault is greater than the second coordination point, coordination succeeds. 

If the upline device is a fuse, then the devices coordinate if the maximum fault is less than the first coordination point. 

If the upline device is a sectionalizer, then the upline device is skipped and the next device upline is considered. 

Any other device is ignored. 

### Sectionalizer 

Defines the device to be a sectionalizer.   

If the upline device is a sectionalizer or a recloser (OCR or Recloser), the minimum pickups are compared and the number of operations are compared. If the sectionalizer’s pickup is less than the upline device’s pickup, derated by 80%, and the upline device has more operations than the downline device, the coordination test passes. 

Any other device is ignored. 

## Phase Operation 

Determines whether this device acts like a three phase device (one phase down then all phases are down) or like a one phase device. For Milsoft’s DisSPatch product only. 

## Current Rating 

The highest current for which this device can be used. 

## Maximum Symmetrical/Asymmetrical Fault 

The highest fault that this device can handle.

## Minimum Pickup 

The smallest fault for which this device will detect and open.

## No of Fast Trip/Slow Trip 

The operations of this device.

## Nominal LG/LL Voltage 

The maximum voltage for which this device is rated. 

Nominal L to G defines the maximum operating nominal line-to-ground voltage for the specified device. If this value is specified, the nominal line-to-line voltage will be calculated by multiplying the line-to-ground voltage by the square root of three. This value is not currently being used; however, we recommend that you enter it if you know it. 

Nominal L to L defines the maximum nominal line-to-line voltage for the specified device. If this value is specified, the nominal line-to-ground voltage will be calculated by dividing the nominal line-to-line voltage by the square root of three. This value is not currently being used; however, we recommend that you enter it if you know it.
transformer:
# Transformer Tab
## Transformer 
Lists the name of the selected transformer equipment. 

## Type 
Lists the type of transformer. 

If “Three Phase Transformer” is selected, you must enter the total three-phase kVA rating is required. 

If “Single Phase Transformer” is selected, the single-phase kVA rating is required and all values will be assumed to be the same for all phases. 

If “--Single Phase Unbalanced--” is selected, the single-phase kVA rating is required and a set of values for each phase is requested. 

If “Three Winding Transformer” is selected, the kVA rating should be a value that is valid for the % Imp entered. 

Tip: “--Single Phase Unbalanced--” is no longer a valid transformer type. Use multiple "Single Phase Transformers" instead. 

## %Imp 

The transformer's percent impedance. 

## X/R 

Specifies the Transformer’s X to R ratio. 

## Three-Phase Rated 

Base kVA and Rated kVA specify the single-phase or three-phase rated kVA for the transformer. 

## No-Load Losses (kW) 

The losses for the transformer. (Tip: When entering a number into this text box, remember that WindMil only allows a number that is at most 10% of the Base kVA.)

#Grounding Data Tab 

Grounding Impedance for the transformer consists of the R (resistance) and X (reactance) for the different types of grounding impedances. All of these values are stated in ohms. 

The options are: 

- Zgp

- Zgs

- Zg
regulator:
## Regulator Name 
The name of the regulator equipment being edited or added. 

## CT Rating 
The CT (primary current transformer) rating for the current regulator. If non-zero, this value will be used to define the Line Drop Compensation base current. If CT Rating is left blank or set to zero, the primary current transformer rating will be set equal to Amp Rating. 

## %Boost 
The maximum percentage boost for the regulator. 

## Step Size 
The step size of the regulator in percent. 

Example: %Boost is “10” and the number of steps is 16. Divide %Boost by the number of steps to get Step Size (Step Size = 10.0/16 = 0.625%). 

## Total Bandwidth 
The bandwidth of the regulator in volts on 120 volt base. 

Example: Bandwidth of regulator is plus or minus 1 Volt on a 120 Volt base. Total Bandwidth = 2 Volts. 

## Boost not Equal to Buck 
Should be selected if this regulator's boost and buck are different.
load_mix:
## Load Mix 
The name of the load mix code that is being edited or added. 

## Constant kVA (PU) 
Defines the per unit ratio of constant kVA load. 

## Constant Impedance (PU) 
Defines the per unit ratio of constant Impedance load. 

## Constant Current (PU) 
Defines the per unit ratio of constant Current load. 

## P 
Designates the kW values for the related fields. 

## Q 
Designates the kVAr values for the related fields. 

## Q = P 
Designates the that the kVAr values are the same as the kW values. 

## Load Connected 
Specifies the way that the load is connected. Wye load is connected line-to-ground. Delta load is connected line-to-line. 

## Example

Using to set a Load Mix definition for 50% constant kVA, 25% constant Impedance, and 25% constant Current, Load settings would be: 

Constant kVA = 0.50

Constant Impedance = 0.25

Constant Current = 0.25
load_zones:
## Load Zone 
Specifies the name of the currently selected load zone. 

## % Growth Rate 
Specifies the growth rate in percent for the current load zone.
assembly:
## Assembly Name 
The name of the assembly as it will appear in the Map Point Editor. 

## Description 
A human-readable description of the assembly. It can be up to 80 characters long. This description will show up in the hint text when you hover your mouse over the assembly name in the Map Point Editor. 

## Assembly Type 
A value chosen from a combo box containing the types shown below. These types are hard-coded and there is no way for you to add additional assembly types to this list. 

 - None 
 - Pole top 
 - Guying 
 - Anchor 
 - Transformer 
 - Grounding 
 - Secondary 
 - Tying 
 - Miscellaneous 
 - Neutral 
 - Protection 
 - Metering 
 - Oil Circuit Recloser 
 - Sectionalizing 
 - Wood 
 - Voltage Alteration 
 - Security Light 
 - Street Light 
 - Traffic Light 
 
## Associated Element Type 
 
While certain assemblies (such as guys and anchors) are not represented by any electrical elements in the circuit model, other assemblies (such as transformer brackets) can be associated with actual elements. For these assembly definitions, it is useful for you specify the type of element (transformer, capacitor, etc.) that each assembly definition represents. Doing this will help the software automatically associate assemblies with the elements they represent when they are added to a map point.
